newsitem.title: CHINA: China shop angers public with Mao Zedong act.
newsitem.headline: China shop angers public with Mao Zedong act.

text.p: Businessmen in eastern China have aroused public fury by hiring actors portraying Chinese leaders to try to attract customers and boost sales, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
One clothing store in the eastern province of Zhejiang had hired two actors to play the late Chairman Mao Zedong and Premier Zhou Enlai at its opening ceremony, Xinhua said.
"When the two performers appeared in grey Chinese tunics on the business occasion, the gathering was infuriated," it said.
One customer told the actors that their actions would harm the images of Mao and Zhou, two of the most revered men in China's pantheon of communist leaders, it said.
The actors, who had played Mao and Zhou on the movie screen, had done promotional gigs for other shops, it said.
"Performers who play Chinese leaders in movies should respect the characters they portray," it said.
China has previously warned actors playing leaders or famous figures not to exploit their roles for personal financial gain.
